description.text: Albemarle Corporation was incorporated in Virginia in 1993. Our principal executive offices are located at 4250 Congress Street, Suite 900, Charlotte, North Carolina 28209. Unless the context otherwise indicates, the terms “Albemarle,” “we,” “us,” “our” or “the Company” mean Albemarle Corporation and its consolidated subsidiaries. Albemarle is a world leader in transforming essential resources into critical ingredients for mobility, energy, connectivity, and health. Our purpose is to enable a more resilient world. We partner to pioneer new ways to move, power, connect, and protect. The end markets we serve include grid storage, automotive, aerospace, conventional energy, electronics, construction, agriculture and food, pharmaceuticals and medical devices. We believe that our world-class resources with reliable and consistent supply, our leading process chemistry, high-impact innovation, customer centricity and focus on people and planet will enable us to maintain a leading position in the industries in which we operate. We and our joint ventures currently operate more than 25 production and research and development (“R&D”) facilities, as well as a number of administrative and sales offices, around the world. As of December 31, 2025, we served approximately 1,900 customers in approximately 70 countries. For information regarding our unconsolidated joint ventures, see Note 8, “Investments,” to our consolidated financial statements included in Part II, Item 8 of this report.

analysis_md:
# ALB — Albemarle Corporation
Engine 5.4 pass-1 run, 2026-10-18. In scope: market cap $11.235B < $40B (key_numbers.md). Price $95.48 (nasdaq_quote_api).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.py output, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
One of the world's largest lithium producers (Energy Storage: Salar de Atacama brine in Chile, Greenbushes and Wodgina hard rock in Australia via JVs, Silver Peak in Nevada) plus a leading bromine / specialty chemicals business (Specialties) and, until the Q1 2026 sale of a 51% controlling stake, the Ketjen refining-catalysts business (now equity income in Corporate). Earnings are dominated by the lithium price: management's own 2026 outlook is framed as three lithium-price scenarios — at ~$10/kg LCE, net sales $4.1–4.3B and adjusted EBITDA $0.9–1.0B; at ~$20/kg, $5.7–6.0B and $2.4–2.6B; at ~$30/kg, $7.5–7.8B and $4.2–4.4B (company 2026 outlook, via search). Q2 2026 printed the recovery: net sales $1.74B (+31.1% YoY), adjusted EBITDA $858.1M (+155%), Energy Storage realized price $19.53/kg LCE (+60.5% YoY) on volumes of 65kT LCE (+11%); management expects 2026 to land toward the high end of the $20/kg scenario, with 2026 Energy Storage volumes of 225–235kT LCE (flat to down ~4%) after the June 9 CGP3 fire at Greenbushes (restarted Aug 1), and full-year 2026 capex guided to ~$500M.

## Owner's earnings
**History (financials_history.csv):** the cycle in one table — FY2022 OE/share $5.23 (revenue $7,320M on the lithium spike), FY2023 −$7.34 (revenue peaked at $9,617M but capex hit $2,154.5M against OCF of $1,326.6M), FY2024 −$8.72 (revenue collapsed to $5,377.5M; OCF $687.9M vs capex $1,680.5M), FY2025 +$5.54 (OCF recovered to $1,282.3M and capex was cut to $589.8M). OE positive in only 2 of the last 5 fiscal years. The engine's normalized base (3-yr median OE/share) is **−$7.34** — the preliminary run therefore printed Tier F / no cash generation on the median window. That median is the distorted base here: it is the middle of a capex-peak / price-trough window (FY2023–FY2025), not the company's current cash generation, so per the STALE_FY procedure the base was rebuilt on TTM figures (below). The method range this creates — F on the filed median, C on TTM — is itself the finding and is reported under Thoughts.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $1,282,267,000 − prior YTD $538,180,000 + current YTD $1,056,241,000 = **TTM $1,800,328,000**
- Capex: FY $589,801,000 − prior YTD $302,252,000 + current YTD $170,407,000 = **TTM $457,956,000**
- SBC: FY $40,271,000 − prior YTD $17,068,000 + current YTD $14,661,000 = **TTM $37,864,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **136,170,000** — this is the filer's own if-converted diluted count from the Q2 2026 10-Q (basic 117,907,000 for H1 2026; diluted 136,170,000 assuming conversion of the mandatory convertible preferred stock now that the company is profitable; in the loss years the same preferred was anti-dilutive, which is why the filed FY diluted counts sit at ~117.6M). The TTM base is therefore on the more conservative, fully-converted denominator.
- **TTM OE total $1,304,508,000 → base OE/share $9.58** (base_source: ttm_json)
- Two quality notes on the TTM window (Q3 2025–Q2 2026): it contains **no** part of the one-time $350M customer prepayment received in January 2025 (that cash sits in FY2025 and flatters the FY2025 OE/share of $5.54, not the TTM base); and its capex leg ($458.0M) runs slightly below the ~$500M full-year 2026 capex guide, i.e. the base is not flattered by a capex holiday — FY2023's $2,154.5M build-out is complete and CGP3 is ramping.
- Maintenance version (financials_history.csv): FY2025 maintenance OE was −$350,277,000 against conservative OE of +$652,195,000 — the gap is the FY2025 GAAP net loss (−$510,628,000, impairment/restructuring-loaded) flowing through the NI-based definition; the OCF-based conservative series is the cleaner one here (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE below).
- Balance sheet: net debt $1.576B at FY2025 (key_numbers.md), 1.40x normalized OE on the engine's diagnostic basis, plus lease liabilities of $127,671,000 (dcf_numbers.json). Stale in the company's favor: in Q1 2026 it repaid $1.3B of debt after the Ketjen sale and reported total debt of $1.9B at March 31, 2026 (Q1 2026 release, via search) — current leverage is materially lower than the FY2025 figure the engine carries.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-to-moderate: tier-1 cost assets, no pricing power
Justification: Tier-1 low-cost assets (Salar de Atacama brine, Greenbushes hard-rock JV, leading bromine position) give a real structural cost advantage, but Albemarle is a commodity price-taker with no pricing power: ROIC (fundamentals.json roic_proxy) ran 8.8% / 6.1% / 8.2% / 21.4% / 1.6% / −11.4% / −2.6% across FY2019–FY2025 — above the cost of capital only in the 2022 lithium spike — and gross margin swung from 42.0% (FY2022) to 12.3% (FY2023), 1.2% (FY2024) and 13.0% (FY2025), recovering to 23.8% on the TTM window in fundamentals.json. A cost-curve position that cannot defend returns through the cycle is a weak-to-moderate moat.
- FOR: Salar de Atacama (Chile) brine and Greenbushes (Australia, JV) hard-rock stake — among the lowest-cost, highest-quality lithium resources in the world. Leading global bromine position (Jordan / Arkansas) with steadier pricing — Specialties Q2 2026 sales +20.5% YoY, adjusted EBITDA +61.3%. Scale and technical know-how in lithium conversion; long-term contracts cover ~40% of lithium salts volume. Balance sheet repaired in the trough: capex cut from $2,154M (FY2023) to $590M (FY2025), $1.3B of debt repaid in Q1 2026, Ketjen 51% stake sold.
- AGAINST: Pure price-taker: realized lithium price swung from the 2022 spike to ~$10/kg in 2025 and back to $19.53/kg realized in Q2 2026 — earnings follow the commodity, not the franchise. Through-cycle ROIC below the cost of capital in most years (FY2023 1.6%, FY2024 −11.4%, FY2025 −2.6%); gross margin 42.0% → 1.2% peak-to-trough. Chinese / African supply overhang and lepidolite capacity cap lithium prices; new supply is the bear case's engine. Heavy capex in expansions: capex of $2,154M in FY2023 against OCF of $1,327M produced negative owner's earnings at the trough. CORFO commissions and the Chilean fiscal take rise with lithium prices, skimming the upside at Atacama.
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-18)
The engine's blended growth is −4.33% (rev CAGR 5y +10.45%, 3y −11.10%, latest rev YoY −4.37%) — a trough-revenue artifact that straddles the price spike and collapse, so scenario starts were set explicitly (offsets −0.057 / −0.007 / +0.063 / +0.103 / +0.143 vs the blend) and the OE multipliers were widened to the company's own price-scenario geometry, with written reasons:
- **Multipliers are lithium-price scenarios, anchored on filed data.** Super bear 0.50× = the actual $10/kg year just filed (FY2025 OE total $652.2M vs TTM $1,304.5M). Bull 1.30× and super bull 1.60× sit inside the company's own $20→$30/kg EBITDA geometry ($2.4–2.6B → $4.2–4.4B, ~1.7×) because CORFO commissions and taxes skim the top. Bear 0.75× is a partial retracement toward ~$15/kg.
- **Growth-start sanity check (mandatory):** every start is below the latest prints — TTM revenue +18.3% YoY (fundamentals.json) and Q2 2026 revenue +31.1% YoY — deliberately: those prints are lithium-*price* recovery off a trough, not volume growth. Volumes are guided flat to down ~4% for 2026 (225–235kT LCE) with CGP3 reaching full run rate only in early 2027, so base growth of +2.0% is a volume-plus-mix assumption at a held ~$20/kg price, not a continuation of the price bounce. Price-level risk is carried in the multipliers, not in compounding growth rates.
- Probabilities 15/25/30/20/10 (defaults shifted 5pp from super bull to super bear): the TTM base already embeds a price recovery, and Chinese supply overhang makes a retracement at least as likely as a spike. Price $95.48.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −10.0% | 0.50 | Lithium back to ~$10/kg and stays (the filed FY2025) | $24.09 | 5.30% |
| Bear | 25% | −5.0% | 0.75 | Price softens toward ~$15/kg on China/Africa supply | $43.97 | 8.00% |
| Base | 30% | 2.0% | 1.00 | ~$20/kg holds; volume-led growth after CGP3 ramp | $76.97 | 12.57% |
| Bull | 20% | 6.0% | 1.30 | $25/kg territory; operating leverage, CORFO skim | $116.63 | 17.68% |
| Super bull | 10% | 10.0% | 1.60 | ~$30/kg sustained plus volume growth | $167.03 | 23.60% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $77.73 (−18.6% vs price), IV@12% $102.41 (+7.3%), IV@10% $129.86, weighted IRR 12.69%, base-case IRR 12.57%**
- **Tier by numbers: C.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 10.03%, terminal value 17.9% of IV@15%, scenario spread 6.93x, net debt 1.40x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY2025 ended 9.6 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted above, on the filer's if-converted diluted share count.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 years): named — it is the lithium price cycle, not a restatement: revenue rose +120% in FY2022 and +31% in FY2023 on the price spike, then fell −44% in FY2024 when prices collapsed (financials_history.csv). The Ketjen deconsolidation (51% sold, closed Q1 2026) is a smaller, real comparability break in the other direction — catalyst revenue leaves the consolidated top line from 2026. Resolution: no CAGR straddling the spike is trusted (the −4.33% blend was overridden with explicit scenario starts, above), and the base is a current cash-flow window, not a growth extrapolation.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2024, 2025): FY2024 net income −$1,179,449,000 vs OCF +$687,876,000 and FY2025 net income −$510,628,000 vs OCF +$1,282,267,000 (financials_history.csv). The wedge is non-cash charges in the trough restructuring (impairments and related charges inside operating income of −$1,776,545,000 in FY2024 and −$367,084,000 in FY2025) plus D&A of $588,638,000 (FY2024) and $658,678,000 (FY2025) — GAAP income understates cash generation in exactly the years the OE base must read. Direction resolved in favor of the OCF-based conservative OE used throughout. One cash-side flatterer is named, not hidden: FY2025 OCF includes the one-time $350M customer prepayment received January 2025 — it affects the FY2025 figure only, not the TTM base (outside its window).
- **CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED**: the FY2025 cash tag is the combined cash + restricted-cash total ($1,618,001,000, financials_history.csv) with no separate restricted-cash tag filed, so the engine's net debt ($1.576B) is understated by the restricted amount, which the computed outputs do not separate out. Materiality is bounded by the post-Q1-2026 balance sheet (total debt $1.9B at March 31, 2026 after the $1.3B repayment, via search): even taking the FY2025 net debt at face value it is 1.40x normalized OE, and the current figure is lower — the flag does not change the verdict, and no HIGH_NET_DEBT conclusion is drawn from the combined-cash figure.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (6.93x): real — it is the lithium cycle expressed in IVs ($24.09 super bear vs $167.03 super bull). Confidence is capped at low and the verdict is sized to the conservative end.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear D 8.00% vs bull B 17.68%): acknowledged — the verdict spans three tiers because the commodity does. Final tier is the weighted C; position sizing, if any, belongs at the bear end.

## My thoughts / overlay
- **Method range is the headline:** F on the filed 3-yr median base (−$7.34/share, a capex-peak/price-trough window), C on the filing-direct TTM base ($9.58/share, weighted IRR 12.69%), and the bull end of that same TTM run reaches B. Anyone quoting one tier for ALB without its base is hiding the cycle.
